newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares take a knock, investors keep away.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares take a knock, investors keep away.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 1.03 percent on Monday as foreign investors continued to huddle on the sidelines, and traders said the market was unlikely to pick up momentum before next month.
"Until foreigners return, the index will continue to decline slowly. I expect it could ease by another five percent by the end of April," said Andrej Obed, a trader at "A" banka.
The Bank of Slovenia in February blocked international investment by saying foreigners have to open custodian accounts at Slovenian banks in order to trade in securities.
But foreigners have so far stayed away, claiming the costs of the new accounts, estimated at about 12 percent of the amount handled, were too high.
Since the central bank's move, the blue chip index has fallen 20.2 percent and average daily volume has slumped to some 60 million tolars from a previous 500 million.
"Although bank interest rates are low, quite a few investors prefer to put their money into banks while waiting for better times on the bourse," a trader said.
The blue-chip SBI index eased 13.72 points to 1,320.88.
Overall 12 shares fell, five rose and 10 were untraded.
Turnover fell to 46.2 million tolars from 47.5 million on Friday.

Aroma producer Etol was the most actively traded issue, rising 1.03 percent to 17,650 tolars on volume of 614 shares. The activity in Etol was a result of Monday being the ex-dividend date, traders said.

Pharmaceutical wholesaler Salus was the leading decliner, falling 10 percent to 13,500 tolars for the second trading day in a row due to its recent announcement that the court procedure regarding the 1990 privatisation process of the company has not yet been concluded.
The Payment Agency last year accused Salus of conducting an irregular privatisation.
"Due to the prolonged court case Salus could fall to between 10,000 and 11,000 tolars," one analyst said.
Ordinary shares of bank Dolenjska banka were the top gainers, up 2.27 percent to 15,300 tolars on volume of 50 shares.
